summary: All round 1 findings correctly addressed. T1-SEC-001 mitigated via explicit template warning. T1-SEC-002 mitigated via explicit key-length requirement in template. Numeric type fix (float→int) is a correctness improvement with no security regression. Task 1 is clear for merge.

round1_findings_resolution.verification: Confirmed in commit 66b2684: template gains a 7-line IMPORTANT block above blogger_telegram_bot_token explaining (a) always edit via `sops <path>`, (b) why — sops leaves empty strings unencrypted, so direct edits would commit the real token in plaintext. The warning is prominent and actionable. The underlying sops behavior (empty string = unencrypted) cannot be changed without sops upstream changes; the warning is the correct mitigation for a template file.
round1_findings_resolution.residual_risk: None beyond the inherent sops convention. The three other empty-string keys (publish_auto_mode_token, blogger_repo_ref, claude_blog_repo_ref) are not high-value secrets when empty — they have no plaintext payload to leak. The token key is the one that matters and it now has the warning.

round1_findings_resolution.verification: Confirmed in commit 66b2684: template gains 4-line addition to publish_callback_hmac_secrets comment: 'Each key segment must be at least 32 bytes of cryptographic randomness (i.e. 64 hex chars from `openssl rand -hex 32`). The worker rejects keys shorter than 32 bytes at startup (loud abort) to prevent silently weakened callback signing.' This documents the contract that Task 6 must enforce. Finding closed at template level; Task 6 implementer is responsible for the runtime validation.

round1_findings_resolution.resolution: NO ACTION REQUIRED — confirmed correct. Round 2 commit re-encrypted publish_min_score and publish_approval_timeout_min with new IVs and updated the file-level MAC. Unique IVs preserved.
DEFERRED TO TASK 8 — noted for bot handler implementer. No action needed in Task 1.

additional_observations.description: publish_min_score and publish_approval_timeout_min were re-encrypted with new IVs (H96HTRA+... and lWXu1rs5... respectively) and the file MAC was recomputed. The new type:int encoding is correct for integer values parsed by Python worker. No security regression; improved type fidelity prevents silent float→int truncation edge cases in Ansible Jinja2 templates.
